'''John Logan Jenkins III''' (born March 6, 1991)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jenkijo01.html|title=John Jenkins NBA & ABA Stats|access-date=February 24, 2016|work=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]] before being selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 23rd pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. He played in the NBA for the Hawks, [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Washington Wizards]] and [[New York Knicks]] from 2012 to 2019. Jenkins has also played professionally in Spain, China, Israel, France, Puerto Rico, Russia and Romania.

==Early life==
As a senior at [[Station Camp High School]], Jenkins was the nation's leading scorer for high schoolers, averaging 42.3 points per game, finishing second on the state's single-season list behind Ronnie Schmitz, who averaged 44.2 points at Ridgeway High School in 1988–89.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jenkins_john00.html|title=John Jenkins Bio|access-date=January 25, 2014|work=VUCommodores.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910170426/http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jenkins_john00.html|archive-date=September 10, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Jenkins was listed as the No. 6 shooting guard and the No. 15 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/66589|title=John Jenkins Recruiting Profile|access-date=January 25, 2014|work=Rivals.com}}</ref> Jenkins was a two-time TSSAA Class AA Mr. Basketball selection, and was the Gatorade Tennessee High School Player of the Year in 2008–09.<ref>{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|url=https://pittsburgh.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=948141|title=Nation's leading scorer preparing for college|work=Rivals.com|date=May 21, 2009|access-date=June 21, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715190344/http://pittsburgh.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=948141|archive-date=July 15, 2011}}</ref>

==College career==
One of the nation's top shooters, Jenkins shot 48.3% (72–149) from three in his freshman season at Vanderbilt, 40.8% (100–245) as a sophomore, and 43.9% (134–305) from beyond-the-arc as a junior. As a sophomore, he led the Southeastern Conference in scoring (19.5) and in 3-point field goals made per game (3.1) and finished second in free throw percentage (.894)<ref name="bio" /> and was picked to the Fifth Team All-America by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010–11 All-America teams |work=FoxSports.com |publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media, LLC |date=March 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 19.9 points per game, leading the SEC for the second consecutive season (the first time since LSU's Ronnie Henderson did it in 1995–96). He also tied an SEC single-season record for threes made in a season with 134. He led the nation in three-pointers made per game (3.9) and was named a third-team All-American by the Associated Press.<ref name="bio" />

On April 9, 2012, Jenkins announced that he would forgo his final year of eligibility at Vanderbilt to enter the [[2012 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/story/2012-04-09/john-jenkins-vanderbilt-nba/54135998/1|title=John Jenkins leaving Vanderbilt a year early for NBA|access-date=April 9, 2012|date=April 9, 2012|work=USAToday.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Atlanta Hawks (2012–2015)===
Jenkins was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 23rd overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-select-john-jenkins-and-mike-scott-2012-nba-draft-0|title=HAWKS SELECT JOHN JENKINS AND MIKE SCOTT IN 2012 NBA DRAFT|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2012|access-date=December 7, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Kris|last=Willis|url=http://atlanta.sbnation.com/atlanta-hawks/2012/6/29/3127146/2012-nba-draft-john-jenkins-danny-ferry|title=2012 NBA Draft: Danny Ferry Discusses John Jenkins, Draft Process|work=SBNation.com|date=June 29, 2012|access-date=June 29, 2012}}</ref> On July 10, 2012, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Hawks<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2012/07/hawks-sign-john-jenkins.html|title=Hawks Sign John Jenkins|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 10, 2012|access-date=July 10, 2012}}</ref> and joined them for the 2012 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/2012-hawks-rookie-camp-and-summer-league-roster|title=2012 HAWKS ROOKIE CAMP AND SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 24, 2016}}</ref> On December 1, 2012, he was assigned to the [[Northern Arizona Suns|Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/atlanta_hawks_assign_john_jenk_2012_12_01.html|title=Atlanta Hawks Assign John Jenkins and Mike Scott to Bakersfield|work=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2012|access-date=December 1, 2012}}</ref> On December 5, 2012, he was recalled by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11632|title=Hawks recall John Jenkins from D-League|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 5, 2012|access-date=December 5, 2012}}</ref>

In July 2013, Jenkins re-joined the Hawks for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On October 31, 2013, the Hawks exercised their third-year team option on Jenkins' rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/230532/Hawks-Exercise-Team-Option-On-John-Jenkins|title=Hawks Exercise Team Option On John Jenkins|work=RealGM.com|date=October 31, 2013|access-date=October 31, 2013}}</ref> On December 6, 2013, he was reassigned to the Bakersfield Jam.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-assign-jenkins-bakersfield-recall-cunningham|title=HAWKS ASSIGN JENKINS, RECALL CUNNINGHAM FROM BAKERSFIELD|work=NBA.com|date=December 6, 2013|access-date=December 6, 2013}}</ref> On December 13, he was recalled by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14914|title=Atlanta Hawks recall John Jenkins from D-League|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 13, 2013|access-date=December 13, 2013}}</ref> Shortly after being recalled, Jenkins was deactivated due to lower back pain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-injury-report-december-27-2013|title=HAWKS INJURY REPORT – DECEMBER 27, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2013|access-date=December 27, 2013}}</ref> On February 3, 2014, the Hawks announced Jenkins underwent successful surgery on his back and subsequently missed the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/john-jenkins-surgery-update|title=JOHN JENKINS SURGERY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=February 3, 2014}}</ref>

In July 2014, Jenkins re-joined the Hawks for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. On October 30, 2014, the Hawks declined to exercise Jenkins' four-year team option and thus allowing him to become an unrestricted free agent in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/235402/Hawks-Decline-John-Jenkins-Fourth-Year-Rookie-Option|title=Hawks Decline John Jenkins' Fourth-Year Rookie Option|work=RealGM.com|date=October 30, 2014|access-date=October 30, 2014}}</ref> On November 28, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/muscala-jenkins-recalled-by-hawks/n-4903181|title=Muscala, Jenkins Recalled by Hawks|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 28, 2014|access-date=November 28, 2014}}</ref> On December 30, 2014, using the flexible assignment rule, the Hawks assigned Jenkins to the [[Idaho Stampede]], the affiliate of the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-assign-john-jenkins-idaho-stampede-and-adreian-payne-austin-spurs|title=Atlanta Hawks Assign John Jenkins To Idaho Stampede and Adreian Payne To Austin Spurs|work=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2014|access-date=December 30, 2014}}</ref> On January 20, 2015, he was recalled by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-recall-john-jenkins-idaho-stampede|title=Hawks Recall John Jenkins from Idaho Stampede|work=NBA.com|date=January 20, 2015|access-date=January 20, 2015}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2015–2016)===
On July 24, 2015, Jenkins signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-john-jenkins-and-jarrid-famous/|title=Mavs sign John Jenkins and Jarrid Famous|work=mavs.com|date=July 24, 2015|access-date=July 24, 2015}}</ref> On October 29, in just his second game for the Mavericks, Jenkins recorded 17 points, 6 rebounds and 3 assists as a starter in a loss to the Los Angeles Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151029/DALLAC/gameinfo.html|title=DeAndre Jordan and Clippers rout Mavs 104–88 in home opener|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151031000408/http://www.nba.com/games/20151029/DALLAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 31, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 22, 2016, he was waived by the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-free-agent-david-lee/|title=Mavericks sign free agent David Lee|work=mavs.com|date=February 22, 2016|access-date=February 22, 2016}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2016–2017)===
On February 24, 2016, Jenkins was claimed off waivers by the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-claim-john-jenkins|title=Suns Claim John Jenkins|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2016|access-date=February 24, 2016}}</ref> The Suns inherited Jenkins' three-year contract with non-guaranteed years of $1.05 million for 2016–17 and $1.18 million for 2017–18.<ref>{{cite news|last=Coro|first=Paul|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2016/07/14/suns-john-jenkins-phoenix-where-want/87082754/|title=Suns' John Jenkins: Phoenix is 'where I want to be'|work=azcentral.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=October 16, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Suns the following day, scoring two points in four minutes off the bench against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160225/BKNPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Bogdanovic, Nets top Suns in battle of lowly teams|work=NBA.com|date=February 25, 2016|access-date=February 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226173635/http://www.nba.com/games/20160225/BKNPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 26, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his first season with the Suns, he averaged 5.0 points and a career-high 1.2 assists per game.

On October 24, 2016, Jenkins was retained by the Suns for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Zimmerman|url=http://arizonasports.com/story/875311/suns-release-archie-goodwin/|title=Suns release guard Archie Goodwin, retain Jenkins and Jones Jr.|work=ArizonaSports.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=December 7, 2016}}</ref> On January 6, 2017, he was waived by the Suns after making four appearances in the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/01/06/suns-waive-john-jenkins|title=Suns waive John Jenkins|work=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2017|access-date=January 6, 2017}}</ref>

===Westchester Knicks (2017)===
On February 3, 2017, Jenkins was acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-acquire-john-jenkins/|title=Westchester Knicks Acquire John Jenkins|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2017|access-date=February 5, 2017}}</ref>

On September 25, 2017, Jenkins signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-shooting-guard-john-jenkins|title=Hawks Sign Shooting Guard John Jenkins|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2017|access-date=September 25, 2017}}</ref> He was waived before the regular season by the Hawks on October 6, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-waive-john-jenkins-jordan-mathews|title=Hawks Waive John Jenkins, Jordan Mathews|work=NBA.com|date=October 6, 2017|access-date=October 6, 2017}}</ref>

===San Pablo Burgos (2017–2018)===
On November 7, 2017, Jenkins signed with Spanish club [[CB Miraflores|San Pablo Burgos]] for his first professional experience in Europe.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=136108|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108202731/http://acb.com/redaccion.php?id=136108|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 8, 2017|publisher=ACB.com|date=November 7, 2017|access-date=November 8, 2017|title=John Jenkins se incorpora a las filas del San Pablo Burgos|language=es}}</ref>

===Westchester Knicks (2018–2019)===
On October 3, 2018, Jenkins signed with the [[New York Knicks]]. He was waived the following day<ref name=realgm>{{cite web |title=John Jenkins Player Profile, New York Knicks - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/John-Jenkins/Summary/2377 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=12 January 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and subsequently joined the Westchester Knicks for the [[2018–19 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2018–19 Training Camp Roster |url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 23, 2018 |date=October 23, 2018 |archive-date=July 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720013334/https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2019)===
On January 30, 2019, Jenkins signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards' John Jenkins: Signs 10-day contract with Wizards|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-john-jenkins-signs-10-day-contract-with-wizards/|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=January 30, 2019}}</ref> During the ten days, he was assigned three times to the [[Capital City Go-Go]].<ref name="realgm" />

===New York Knicks (2019)===
On February 11, 2019, Jenkins signed a 10-day contract with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite tweet |user=NY_KnicksPR |number=1095002382872834049 |date=February 11, 2019 |title=New York Knicks signed guard John Jenkins of @wcknicks to a 10-day contract}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=New York Knicks Sign John Jenkins to 10-Day Contract |url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/new-york-knicks-sign-john-jenkins-to-10-day-contract/ |website=gleague.nba.com |access-date=February 12, 2019 |date=February 11, 2019 |archive-date=February 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190212190534/https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/new-york-knicks-sign-john-jenkins-to-10-day-contract/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He signed a rest-of-season contract on February 21.<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Knicks Sign John Jenkins |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-sign-john-jenkins |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 21, 2019 |date=February 21, 2019}}</ref>

===Jiangsu Dragons (2020)===
In January 2020, Jenkins joined the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]..<ref>{{cite web|title=John Jenkins joins Jiangsu Dragons|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/610607/John-Jenkins-joins-Jiangsu-Dragons|date=January 6, 2020|website=asia-basket.com|access-date=January 6, 2020}}</ref>

===Hapoel Eilat (2020)===
On February 26, 2020, Jenkins signed with [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/john-jenkins-signs-with-hapoel-eilat/|title=John Jenkins signs with Hapoel Eilat|date=February 26, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 26, 2020|last1=Carchia|first1=Emiliano}}</ref>

===Bilbao Basket (2020–2021)===
On December 15, 2020, Jenkins signed a two-month contract with [[Bilbao Basket|RETAbet Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bilbao-signs-john-jenkins/|title=Bilbao signs John Jenkins|date=December 15, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=December 15, 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref> He averaged 12.6 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.2 assists per game.<ref name="Gravelines" />

===BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque (2021–2022)===
In August 2021, Jenkins signed with [[BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref name="Gravelines">{{cite web |title=Gravelines land John Jenkins, ex Bilbao |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/702413/Gravelines-land-John-Jenkins,-ex-Bilbao |website=Eurobasket |access-date=August 29, 2021 |date=August 29, 2021}}</ref>

===NBA G League Ignite (2022–2023)===
In September 2022, Jenkins joined the [[NBA G League Ignite]] for the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/ignite-announces-veteran-roster-additions/n-5885964|title=Ignite Announces Veteran Roster Additions|website=oursportscentral.com|date=September 28, 2022|access-date=September 28, 2022}}</ref>

===Bàsquet Girona (2023)===
On March 30, 2023, Jenkins signed with [[Bàsquet Girona]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basquetgirona.com/senior/es/actualidad/john-jenkins-ficha-por-el-basquet-girona.html|title=John Jenkins ficha por el Bàsquet Girona|last=|first=|date=March 30, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=March 30, 2023}}</ref>

===Return to the NBA G League Ignite (2023–2024)===
Jenkins re-joined the [[NBA G League Ignite]] for the [[2023–24 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ignite Announces Veteran Roster Additions For 2023-24 Season|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/ignite-announces-veteran-roster-additions-for-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=August 28, 2023|access-date=August 28, 2023}}</ref>

===Criollos de Caguas (2024)===
On May 26, 2024, Jenkins signed with [[Criollos de Caguas (basketball)|Criollos de Caguas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR {{¡}} ÚLTIMA HORA: El escolta ex-NBA John Jenkins es el nuevo refuerzo de los Criollos de Caguas en sustitución de Louis King. Jenkins tiene 32 años, mide 6'4 y viene de promediar 18 PPJ y 49% en triples con el club G-League Ignite.|number=1794865138543268246|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=May 26, 2024|access-date=May 26, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Lokomotiv Kuban (2025)===
In March 2025, Jenkins joined [[Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]] for the rest of the 2024–25 season.<ref name=Eurobasket>{{cite web |title=John Jenkins |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/John-Jenkins/188794 |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=12 January 2026 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Cangrejeros de Santurce (2025)===
Jenkins joined [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] for the [[2025 Baloncesto Superior Nacional season]].<ref name="Eurobasket" />

===CS Vâlcea 1924 Râmnicu Vâlcea (2025–2026)===
In December 2025, Jenkins joined [[CS Vâlcea 1924 Râmnicu Vâlcea]] of the Romanian [[Liga Națională (men's basketball)|Liga Națională]].<ref name="Eurobasket" /> He played five games for Vâlcea between December 13 and January 10.<ref name="Eurobasket" />

===Adelaide 36ers and Santeros de Aguada (2026–present)===
On January 14, 2026, Jenkins signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the rest of the [[2025–26 NBL season|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=36ers add scoring guard |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/adelaide-36ers-add-scoring-guard-john-jenkins |access-date=14 January 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=14 January 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2026, Jenkins joined [[Santeros de Aguada]] for the rest of the 2026 BSN season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Modestti |first1=Luis |title=John Jenkins (ex Adelaide) agreed terms with Aguada |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto%20Rico/news/992780/John-Jenkins-(ex-Adelaide)-agreed-terms-with-Aguada |access-date=22 June 2026 |work=latinbasket.com |date=28 May 2026}}</ref>

On June 22, 2026, Jenkins re-signed with the 36ers for the [[2026–27 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=36ers complete roster with key import secured |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/36ers-complete-nbl27-roster-with-key-import-secured |access-date=22 June 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=22 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
